title: 先核对无dropout的循环训练配方

material_passport.Verification Status: UNVERIFIED method effect; recipe/source comparison only

authorization.scope: Recipe audit and concrete design only

positioning: A standard-recipe adaptation and single-factor extension of the existing Loop stability question, not a new algorithm or an established mechanism repair. Prefer verifying this simple difference before adding the adversarial inner loop; do not automatically stack changes.
observations: At fixed native EMA/R8, B4 falls 71.24% to 5.66% between 256k and 500k. At R4/R8 both atomic pools and trained A compositions remain mastered; training A4 answer NLL falls from approximately 1.4e-5 to 3e-6 at R8.

Within the 4189 queries with a correct decoded first bridge at R1 in both checkpoints, second-hop candidate accuracy falls 88.78% to 24.90%. This is a descriptive conditioned subset, not a causal effect estimate. The regression is not solely a first-hop reception problem.

At 500k, the true-bridge atomic whole-post-attention donor improves second-hop candidate accuracy 21.16% to 99.98%, but final B4 only 5.66% to 27.96%. It demonstrates a material calling-state bottleneck, not its training cause, and does not establish a local perturbation radius.
Existing evaluation and donor diagnoses already disable dropout. The observed evaluation failure is in the learned weights; changing an evaluation flag cannot undo it.

recipe_comparison.aspect: Task supervision and recurrent gradient horizon
recipe_comparison.ours: Original answer/EOS CE at two segment ends, averaged equally. First segment 4-6 loops, second 1-4; carry detached between segments. Random lengths are already present.
recipe_comparison.huginn: Ordinary language-model endpoint objective over sampled heavy-tailed depths; backpropagation through the final eight iterations. This differs from our two-loss/two-segment objective, not merely a missing switch.
recipe_comparison.ouro: Multi-depth next-token CE weighted by learned exit probabilities, with exit-distribution entropy regularization and a separate gate-training phase.
recipe_comparison.decision: Keep our existing schedule and objective for the first controlled comparison. Do not claim we lack random depth or deep supervision, or add Ouro's exit objective to solve a different problem.

recipe_comparison.aspect: Dropout and conditioning across one trajectory
recipe_comparison.ours: Attention, residual and embedding dropout all 0.1. Each run() recomputes _embedded(tokens); the second supervised segment injects a freshly sampled dropped embedding while carrying the first segment's state. Attention and residual masks also resample across block calls.
recipe_comparison.huginn: Author-provided dynamic model has no embedding/residual dropout on the checked path. Its supplied 512-node launch selects the tridao backend, whose actual attention call passes dropout_p=0.0.
recipe_comparison.ouro: Official released model config uses attention_dropout=0.0, and the released architecture has no embedding/residual dropout. Complete historical pretraining stage configs were not independently retrieved.
recipe_comparison.decision: Test setting all three current probabilities to zero as the only scientific change. This removes this source of intra-trajectory stochasticity and the segment input-mask change, without claiming that either was already proven harmful.

recipe_comparison.ours: Pre-LN Transformer block, normalized feedback/candidate and normalized history aggregation; raw token+position input reinjection. MLP already receives LN2(u).
recipe_comparison.huginn: Post-residual sandwich RMSNorm, trained input-state adapter and scaled input embeddings.
recipe_comparison.ouro: The released block normalizes attention/MLP branch outputs before residual addition; the exact formula differs from Huginn despite the shared sandwich name.
recipe_comparison.decision: A genuine architectural difference, not proof of the observed cause. Do not bundle it into this comparison or claim that our MLP originally sees an unnormalized input. Old norm-handoff changed a different boundary and lacks formal scientific training endpoints.

recipe_comparison.ours: AdamW, betas=(0.9,0.95), weight decay 0.1 with existing exclusions, gradient clip 1, peak LR 1e-4, warmup 2000, cosine horizon 1.5m, EMA 0.999.
recipe_comparison.huginn: The supplied 512-node launch uses ELLISAdam at 4e-5 with update clipping and its own decoupled-decay conventions; raw coefficient values are not directly comparable to ours.
recipe_comparison.ouro: AdamW, the same listed betas/decay/clip family, but its own large-batch, staged LR and loop-depth recipe.
recipe_comparison.decision: No evidence currently identifies gradient explosion as the cause of low-loss composition regression. Retain original optimization; do not copy a numerical LR or decay coefficient across implementations.

hypothesis.statement: Training a single dropout-free recurrent computation may preserve reusable calling behavior better than optimizing over resampled internal masks in this recipe.
hypothesis.specific_link: Calls are repeatedly composed. Fresh internal masks, including a newly sampled conditioning embedding between segments, create training trajectories that differ from the dropout-free inference trajectory. Existing observations motivate checking this plausible optimization factor, but do not prove it explains second-hop content mismatch.
hypothesis.not_a_bug_claim: Ordinary inverted dropout intentionally differs between train and evaluation. The current implementation is not declared incorrect. Removing dropout also removes regularization and changes the optimization trajectory.
hypothesis.scope_of_consistency: The mathematical block has no dropout noise for fixed parameters/input; minibatch sampling, random loop lengths, AdamW and finite-precision kernel behavior remain. This is not bitwise deterministic training or a convergence guarantee.

proposed_change.implementation_note: Create a new immutable experiment config only after execution authorization. Configure before model construction so GPT-2 MLP dropout modules and functional attention/residual/embedding dropout all receive zero. Do not use model.eval() as a training shortcut.
preserve: Same state-MLP gate, all trainable parameters, tied embeddings, full residual/attention/MLP/LayerNorm, feedback and aggregation
Original data panels and A-composition/B-atomic exposure; no true intermediate entity, hop identity, graph ID or B-composition labels added
Two original random segment lengths, answer/EOS CE, equal segment loss weights and carry detach
Original initialization, data/schedule seeds, batch size, optimizer, LR horizon, clipping, checkpoint protocol and EMA
proposed_change.no_additions: No adversarial passes, extra loss, teacher model, activation perturbation, replay bank, extra parameters, inferred intermediate label or new inference rule.

arms: Reuse the original dropout=0.1 state-MLP trajectory as the comparator.
One new dropout=0 training from exactly the original step-zero weights to 500k updates.
proposed_development_comparison.lr_contract: Keep the original 1.5m cosine horizon even though development evaluation ends at 500k. Do not shorten the schedule.
proposed_development_comparison.recovery_contract: Historical 256k snapshots do not contain matching full optimizer/RNG states. Do not claim an exact historical continuation or reuse that curve as an optimizer-reset comparator.
proposed_development_comparison.primary: Unperturbed EMA/R8 B4 accuracy at the fixed 500k endpoint, plus the full 256k/300k/400k/500k trajectory and its minimum. Improvement must not be inferred from a flatter near-zero curve or a best-checkpoint selection.
proposed_development_comparison.preservation: Atomic A/B and A2-A4 performance, B2/B3, raw and EMA separately, and fixed R8/R16 behavior with gains/losses of original correct answers. Lower training loss alone is not success.
proposed_development_comparison.diagnosis: Repeat the existing zero-training second-hop measurements at the fixed endpoints. A first-hop-only gain while the common-bridge second-hop failure persists is not evidence that the main calling regression was repaired. True-bridge interventions remain evaluation-only.
proposed_development_comparison.compute: Same data and loop schedule imply the same nominal matrix FLOPs and repeated exposures. Track actual tokens, examples, GPU-hours and resource sharing. No extra forward/backward passes; kernel selection and real speed can differ.
proposed_development_comparison.interpretation: One known world and initialization provide development evidence. A gain estimates the effect of removing the combined dropout recipe, not a uniquely identified effect of operator variation versus conditioning masks versus regularization.
proposed_development_comparison.failure: If training loss decreases but native B4 still regresses, or removing regularization increases composition overfitting, the proposal fails its purpose. Do not automatically add normalization, shorter-depth supervision, learning-rate changes or an adversarial inner loop.

validation_before_any_future_run: Verify only the three dropout config values differ; original zero-step parameter hashes, data and schedule streams match.
Verify no active nonzero dropout remains, including the constructed GPT-2 MLP dropout module; fixed-weight/fixed-depth train/eval computations agree within numerical kernel tolerances.
Preserve causal attention, original answer/EOS masking and two-segment loss/gradient structure. Do not detach the embedding or add new labels.
Check independent reload and resumable optimizer/data/schedule/RNG/EMA state in the new batch before formal execution.

checked: Loop reports/results/protocols searched for dropout controls
history_check.finding: Older zero-dropout tasks and recipes exist, with multiple other differences; they are not a controlled comparison for this same state-MLP world and schedule. No clean 0.1-to-0 paired scientific result was found in the checked records.
history_check.boundary: Do not call dropout-zero a novel algorithm or claim that the entire repository has never used it. Existing gate/KV/position/normalization results remain unchanged.

scalability.large_model_requirements: Ordinary task or next-token supervision suffices. The change introduces no extra teacher, entity labels, inner optimization or depth-dependent storage. It does not remove the underlying recurrence cost.
scalability.unverified: This establishes low engineering overhead, not improved large-LLM knowledge composition. The tiny, repeatedly exposed dataset may benefit from dropout regularization, so large-corpus precedent is not an effectiveness guarantee here.

primary_external_sources.name: Ouro original paper, latest revision checked

source_limits: Huginn author repository main was inspected, not pinned to an independently recovered historical training commit or runtime dump.
Ouro released configuration is not treated as an independent audit of every historical pretraining stage.
No training or zero-dropout repair was performed in this design turn.
